previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A 60-year-old woman with mast cell degranulation syndrome was admitted for a recurrent mast cell flare characterized by chest pain, shortness of breath, itching, abdominal pain, and nausea, following a recent discharge for similar symptoms. She was treated with intravenous diphenhydramine, hydromorphone, and lorazepam on her usual every-four-hour protocol, with symptomatic relief. Her course was marked by relapsing symptoms despite stable vital signs and no evidence of infection or cardiac ischemia. A chest X-ray showed stable findings with known nodular opacities, and biopsy results from a prior admission confirmed organizing pneumonia without malignancy, which was reassuring. She remained hemodynamically stable, tolerated oral intake, and was discharged home after a safety delay post-IV medication administration. Follow-up was arranged with pulmonology and rheumatology to discuss lung nodule management and potential restart of etanercept, with no changes to her home medications.

radiology_notes.text:
INDICATION:  Cough and fever, evaluate for pneumonia.

COMPARISON:  Chest radiographs from ___.

FINDINGS:  The right venous infusion catheter ends near the superior
cavoatrial junction.  The cardiac and mediastinal contours are normal.  There
are unchanged calcified lymph nodes in the AP window.  Nodular opacities in
the retrocardiac area correlate with findings on CT from ___. 
One of these nodules was previously biopsied and demonstrated organizing
pneumonia.  The lungs are otherwise clear.  There are no pleural
abnormalities.

IMPRESSION:
Persistent nodular opacities in the retrocardiac area are likely organizing
pneumonia as determined by recent biopsy.  Continued surveillance of these
lesions is recommended to ensure resolution.

CHEST CT

HISTORY:  Rheumatoid arthritis, mast cell activating syndrome, left nodules
biopsied in ___ showed organizing pneumonia.  Assess for any change.

TECHNIQUE:  Multidetector helical scanning of the chest was performed without
intravenous contrast agent reconstructed as contiguous 5- and 1.25-mm thick
axial and 5-mm thick coronal and parasagittal images compared to chest CT on
___ and read in conjunction with subsequent chest radiographs.

FINDINGS:

The mass-like consolidative lesion in the left lower lobe at the junction of
superior and posterior basal segments has shrunk from 21 x 25 mm to 18 x 14
mm, 4:33, and at its periphery, a very small region of cavitation has
increased, consistent with involution of the lesion.  In the vicinity,
clusters of bronchiolar nodules have also grown smaller and less numerous,
including what might have been a second lesion, previously 8 x 5 mm now 3 x 4
mm, 4:32.  What was clearly a third lesion, in the lingula adjacent to a
calcified granuloma, previously 21 x 15 mm, has substantially cleared with a
residual of peribronchial infiltration around mildly dilated distal bronchi. 
The appearance of both major lesions is consistent with involuting pneumonia
infectious or cryptogenic.

New, however, is heterogeneity in the background density of the basal segments
of both lower lobes, more suggestive of new ground-glass opacity in some
regions, rather than hyperinflation in others.  I would like to confirm this
with expiratory views with the patient prone.  A 4-mm wide subpleural left
lower lobe nodule was probably smaller in ___, though measurement of
nodules this small is difficult.

A 10-mm wide right lower paratracheal lymph node, with attenuation of 22 ___,
was 12 mm with attenuation of 4 ___ in ___.  There are no other
pathologically enlarged lymph nodes except for a large calcified lymph node in
the AP window.  There is no pericardial or pleural effusion.  Central venous
catheter ends in the upper right atrium, as before.

This study is not designed for subdiaphragmatic evaluation except to note the
spleen has two persistent incompletely characterized low-density lesions, new
since an abdomen CT on ___, and it contains calcified granulomas
and calcifications in lymph nodes at the hilus. Atherosclerotic calcification
in the splenic artery and normal caliber abdominal aorta is mild to moderate
in extent.

IMPRESSION:
1.  Substantial involution over five weeks in two similar-appearing left lung
nodules, one biopsied, and possibly a third, smaller lesion, as well as
bronchiolar nodules in the vicinity. This regression is perfectly consistent
with organizing pneumonia, either infectious or cryptogenic.
2.  Suggest expiratory images in the prone position to distinguish new areas
of alveolitis or hemorrhage from intervening areas of obstructive lung.
3.  Slight growth of a 4-mm left lower lobe nodule, probably unrelated to the
resolving lesions. Should be followed with a Chest CT in six months.
4.  Granulomatous calcifications in the lung, mediastinal lymph nodes and
spleen.  No good evidence for active mycobacterial infection.
5.  Low-density splenic lesions, probably new since an abdomen CT on ___, should be evaluated by ultrasound.
